newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks edge down on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks edge down on political worries.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange showed small losses overall Monday in apathetic trade marked by investor concern over Peru's internal politics and unstable relations with neighboring Ecuador, brokers said.
They predicted a similar trend for Tuesday.
According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index fell 0.43 percent to 2,160.89 points while the blue- chip Selective Index was off 0.55 percent to 3,102.98.

"It has been a very quiet, apathetic day. There is a lack of enthusiasm from investors due to the political situation and the news about relations with Ecuador," said Guillermo Siles, of Argos brokerage.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori has seen his popularity dive in recent weeks to a record low on his perceived authoritarianism, while media reports have played up tensions on the disputed border with Ecuador.
Brokers said that some mining stocks bucked Monday's trend, boosted by world zinc prices.
Miner Morococha, for example, gained 1.63 percent to 6.25 soles, while another miner Atacocha rose 0.85 percent to 2.38 soles.
Brewery group Unin de Cerveceras Peruanas Backus y Johnston accounted for most volume on the bolsa, with 1.1 shares traded as it closed down 0.36 percent to 2.74.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru also dipped, by 1.88 percent, to 6.77 soles, while another leader Luz del Sur ended off 0.96 percent to 3.10 soles.
Manuel Bustamante, of Investa brokerage, said the economy's healthy long-term projections, should help breath back life into the bolsa soon.
"After expectations drop regarding internal politics and Ecuador, investors will return to Peruvian stocks," he said.
Overall Monday, 35 stocks fell, 30 were flat and 29 rose.
